data.name: Belphoebe
data.gender_notes: Belphoebe is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Greek 'belos' (beautiful) and 'phoebe' (marsh dweller or shining one). This name was borne by the nymph who was the daughter of the goddess Proserpina and the river god Styx, and was the goddess of fertility, bees, and the countryside. The name Belphoebe carries the meaning “Beautiful Marsh Dweller” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Belphoebe usually hope their child will grow to embody beautiful marsh dweller and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that embodies beauty, nature, and the divine. Belphoebe is a reminder to cherish the natural world and to bring beauty into our lives through our actions and intentions.
data.etymology: Belphoebe belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Beautiful Marsh Dweller.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Belphoebe total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: Belphoebe is a rare, evocative, and beautiful name rooted in classical mythology, invoking images of the beauty of nature and the grace of mythological beings. It also has associations with the ancient belief in the protective powers of bees.
data.spiritual_significance: Belphoebe is a name that represents the beautiful and divine aspects of nature, invoking a sense of reverence and awe. As a name associated with the goddess of fertility, it embodies the life-giving and nurturing qualities of the earth, as well as the potential for renewal and growth. Additionally, the name's association with the goddess of bees can carry the symbolism of hard work, collaboration, and the sweet rewards of labor. In spiritual practices, Belphoebe can be a reminder of the importance of honoring the beauty and abundance of nature, and the relevance of the divine in our daily lives.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Belphoebe is a name derived from Greek mythology, meaning "beautiful as a goddess" or "shining darkness." In Christian symbolism, it represents the radiant light of faith shining through the challenges of life, even amidst the darkest moments. It is a reminder of the power of faith to transform and illuminate our world.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Belphoebe was a nymph in Greek mythology, known for her beauty and grace. The name Belphoebe carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
Belphoebe is mentioned in Shakespeare's 'Two Noble Kinsmen' as a shepherdess who is in love with the shepherd Silvius.
